title: Spherical electrovacuum mass and local rigidity

items.title: Spherical orbit geometry and rotational invariance

references.title: K. A. Bronnikov, S.-W. Kim and M. V. Skvortsov, The Birkhoff theorem and string clouds, arXiv:1604.04905v1 (2016)
references.locator: Section 2, equation (1), PDF pp. 2–3: the local spherically symmetric warped metric and areal-radius variable; the source uses signature (+---).

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: Section 6.1.1, printed pp. 234–236 (PDF pp. 241–243): the local spherical quotient metric, its areal-radius function, and the restrictions of the coordinate argument.

items.statement:
Let $U$ be a nonempty, connected, simply connected, second-countable smooth
two-manifold without boundary. Let $q$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $U$ such that $q_y$ is nondegenerate of signature $(-,+)$
for every $y\in U$. Choose a smooth vector field $N$ on $U$ with
$q(N,N)<0$ everywhere; the **time orientation** is the choice of the
connected component containing $N_y$ in each timelike cone
$\{v\in T_yU:q_y(v,v)<0\}$. Choose an orientation of $U$, and let
$\epsilon_2$ be its metric volume form, characterized by
$\epsilon_2(e_0,e_1)=1$ on every positively oriented $q$-orthonormal frame
with $q(e_0,e_0)=-1$ and $q(e_1,e_1)=1$. Let $r:U\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth.
Take $S^2=\{p\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot p=1\}$ with the smooth structure and
induced round metric fixed by the earlier dyonic Reissner–Nordström data
definition cited below. Its tangent plane is
$T_pS^2=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:p\cdot u=0\}$, its metric is
$\gamma_{S^2,p}(u,v)=u\cdot v$, and its outward area form is
$(\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v)=\det(p,u,v)$. Write $\wedge$ for the exterior
product of alternating forms. In polar coordinates
$\omega_{S^2}=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. Put
$\mathcal M:=U\times S^2$ and define its projections by
$\pi_U(y,p):=y$ and $\pi_S(y,p):=p$. For a smooth map $F:X\to Y$ and a
smooth covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ on $Y$, define its pullback by
$$(F^*h)_x(v,w):=h_{F(x)}(dF_xv,dF_xw),$$
where $x\in X$, $v,w\in T_xX$, and $dF_x:T_xX\to T_{F(x)}Y$ is the
derivative. This formula also defines pullback of a covariant $2$-form.
Define
$$g:=\pi_U^*q+(r\circ\pi_U)^2\pi_S^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$
It has Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$.
The fibre over $y\in U$ is $S^2_y:=\pi_U^{-1}(\{y\})=\{y\}\times S^2$.
Its induced Riemannian metric is $r(y)^2\gamma_{S^2}$ and its area form is
$r(y)^2\omega_{S^2}$; in polar angles $0<\theta<\pi$ and
$0\le\phi<2\pi$, its area is
$\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi r(y)^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi=4\pi r(y)^2$.
Thus $r(y)>0$ is the areal radius of this orbit sphere.
Choose the four-dimensional orientation so that its metric volume form is
$$\mathrm{vol}_g=-(r\circ\pi_U)^2\,\pi_U^*\epsilon_2\wedge\pi_S^*\omega_{S^2}.$$
In any chart $(x^0,r)$ for which $\epsilon_2=-dx^0\wedge dr$, this gives
$\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dr\wedge r^2\omega_{S^2}$.

Define
$$SO(3):=\{R\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}:R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3,\ \det R=1\}.$$
Each $R\in SO(3)$ acts on $S^2$ by $p\mapsto Rp$ and defines the smooth
diffeomorphism $\rho_R:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$,
$\rho_R(y,p)=(y,Rp)$, whose inverse is $\rho_{R^{\mathsf T}}$.
For nonnegative integers $a,b$, a smooth tensor field of type $(a,b)$ on
$\mathcal M$ is a smooth section of
$$T^a_b\mathcal M:=(T\mathcal M)^{\otimes a}\otimes(T^*\mathcal M)^{\otimes b};$$
at each $x\in\mathcal M$ its value is multilinear on $a$ covectors in
$T_x^*\mathcal M$ and $b$ vectors in $T_x\mathcal M$, where
$T_x^*\mathcal M:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(T_x\mathcal M,\mathbb R)$.
Smoothness means that the components of the section in every smooth product
chart are $C^\infty$. For such a field $T$, define its pullback by the
diffeomorphism $\rho_R$ by
$$(\rho_R^*T)_x(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_a;v_1,\ldots,v_b)=T_{\rho_R(x)}(\alpha_1\circ(d\rho_R)_x^{-1},\ldots,\alpha_a\circ(d\rho_R)_x^{-1};(d\rho_R)_xv_1,\ldots,(d\rho_R)_xv_b)$$
where $\alpha_i\in T_x^*\mathcal M$, $v_j\in T_x\mathcal M$, and
$(d\rho_R)_x:T_x\mathcal M\to T_{\rho_R(x)}\mathcal M$ is the derivative
of $\rho_R$ at $x$.
A real two-form is a smooth alternating tensor field of type $(0,2)$.
The field $T$ is **rotationally invariant** if $\rho_R^*T=T$ for every
$R\in SO(3)$; a two-form $\mathcal F$ is rotationally invariant in exactly
this sense. This definition specifies a local warped-product model and a
group action. No embedding into a larger spacetime, global potential, maximal
extension, or field equation is assumed.

items.title: Source-free rotational Maxwell fields have constant fluxes

references.title: K. A. Bronnikov, S.-W. Kim and M. V. Skvortsov, The Birkhoff theorem and string clouds, arXiv:1604.04905v1 (2016)
references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 1 proof, PDF pp. 3–4: spherical source-free Maxwell fields carry constant electric and magnetic flux parameters.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: Section 6.2.1, printed pp. 259–260 (PDF pp. 266–267): electric and magnetic flux conventions for the Reissner–Nordström field.

items.statement:
Assume the geometry and orientation of the preceding spherical orbit
definition and countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If a smooth
rotationally invariant real two-form $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal M=U\times S^2$
satisfies
$d\mathcal F=0$ and $d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$, then there are unique constants
$q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$\mathcal F=\frac{q_e}{r^2}\pi_U^*\epsilon_2+q_m\pi_S^*\omega_{S^2}.$$
For every orbit sphere $S_y=\{y\}\times S^2$ the constants are the signed
fluxes with normalization
$$q_e=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S_y}\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S_y}\mathcal F.$$
The proof uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ only through the supplied global flux
integration convention; its local algebra and differential-form calculation
make no use of full choice.

items.statement:
Let $(U,q,\epsilon_2)$ be a connected, oriented, time-oriented smooth
two-dimensional Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+)$ with
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.
In local coordinates $y^0,y^1$, define
$$\Gamma^A{}_{BC}:=\frac12q^{AD} (\partial_Bq_{DC}+\partial_Cq_{BD}-\partial_Dq_{BC}),$$
and use the resulting metric-selected derivative $\nabla^q$ and the
curvature convention
$$R^A{}_{BCD}:=\partial_C\Gamma^A{}_{DB}-\partial_D\Gamma^A{}_{CB} +\Gamma^A{}_{CE}\Gamma^E{}_{DB}-\Gamma^A{}_{DE}\Gamma^E{}_{CB}.$$
Let $\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{BD}:=q^{AC}q_{AE}R^E{}_{BCD}$ and
$S_q:=q^{BD}\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{BD}$. Then
$$\nabla^q\epsilon_2=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}(q)=\frac12S_q\,q.$$
The only inherited choice assumption is $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from the
four-dimensional Levi-Civita supplier used below; no full axiom of choice is
used.

items.title: Spherical electrovacuum quotient and charged mass

references.title: K. A. Bronnikov, S.-W. Kim and M. V. Skvortsov, The Birkhoff theorem and string clouds, arXiv:1604.04905v1 (2016)
references.locator: Section 3, Theorem 1 and equations (8)–(9), PDF pp. 3–4: four-dimensional spherical electrovac equations, charge parameters, and the Reissner–Nordström–(A)dS family.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: Sections 6.2.1 and 6.2.5, printed pp. 259–260 and 266–268 (PDF pp. 266–267 and 273–275): dyonic RN flux conventions and the Bertotti–Robinson exceptional product.

items.statement:
An exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–$\Lambda$ datum consists of the orbit
geometry specified above, a smooth rotationally invariant real two-form
$\mathcal F$, a constant $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and
the equations
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}(g)_{ab}=\Lambda g_{ab}+2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F),$$
where
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c -\frac14g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd}.$$
This is a mathematical system of equations, not a physical postulate. For
$\Lambda=0$ it uses exactly the curvature, Hodge, and Maxwell normalization of
the previously defined geometric electrovac equations. For $\Lambda\ne0$ the extra constant
term is part of this local mathematical definition; it is not supplied by
that zero-$\Lambda$ item.

By the preceding Maxwell reduction lemma, the field has unique constant
flux parameters $q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ and
$$\mathcal F=\frac{q_e}{(r\circ\pi_U)^2}\pi_U^*\epsilon_2+q_m\pi_S^*\omega_{S^2},\qquad Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2.$$
In subsequent formulas on $\mathcal M$, a tensor or differential form on
$U$ or $S^2$ written without a pullback symbol denotes its pullback by
$\pi_U$ or $\pi_S$, respectively; a scalar on $U$ denotes its composition
with $\pi_U$. Formulas stated on $U$ retain their original base objects.
In geometric units, coordinates have length, $r,q_e,q_m$ have length, the
metric components are dimensionless, and $\Lambda$ has units of inverse
length squared. Define
$$z:=q^{-1}(dr,dr),\qquad \varpi:=\frac r2(1-z)+\frac{Q^2}{2r}-\frac{\Lambda r^3}{6}.$$
Thus $z$ is dimensionless and $\varpi$ has length. The scalar $\varpi$ is
called the charged spherical mass function; this definition does not assert
that it is constant. The field equations are local on $U\times S^2$ and
impose no global potential, bundle, horizon, asymptotic, completeness, or
extension condition.

The geometric-electrovacuum flux convention inherits only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
through the supplied geometric electrovac definition. No full axiom of choice is used
by this definition or by the subsequent local algebra.

items.title: Warped two-sphere curvature and charged mass conservation

references.title: K. A. Bronnikov, S.-W. Kim and M. V. Skvortsov, The Birkhoff theorem and string clouds, arXiv:1604.04905v1 (2016)
references.locator: Sections 2–3, equations (3), (8) and (9), PDF pp. 2–4: the spherical Einstein equations and radial Maxwell stress; all warped-product component formulas below are derived locally.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: Sections 3.2.2 and 3.4.1, printed pp. 105–108 and 130–131 (PDF pp. 112–115 and 137–138): curvature sign, Ricci contraction, and curvature identities.

items.statement:
For an exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–$\Lambda$ datum, let
$z=q^{-1}(dr,dr)$ and
$\Delta_qr:=q^{AB}(\nabla^q_A dr)_B$. The warped metric
$g=q+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$ has
$$\operatorname{Ric}(g)_{AB} =\operatorname{Ric}(q)_{AB}-2r^{-1}(\nabla^q_A dr)_B,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}(g)_{ij}=(1-z-r\Delta_qr)\gamma_{ij},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}(g)_{Ai}=0.$$
Its Maxwell tensor satisfies
$$Q_{AB}(\mathcal F)=-\frac{Q^2}{2r^4}q_{AB},\qquad Q_{ij}(\mathcal F)=\frac{Q^2}{2r^4}g_{ij},\qquad Q_{Ai}(\mathcal F)=0.$$
Consequently the Einstein–Maxwell–$\Lambda$ equations imply
$$\nabla^q_A dr_B=\frac12(\Delta_qr)q_{AB},\qquad \Delta_qr=\frac{1-z}{r}-\Lambda r-\frac{Q^2}{r^3},\qquad d\varpi=0.$$

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let an exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–$\Lambda$
datum be given on a connected patch. Suppose $dr$ is nowhere zero and
$z=q^{-1}(dr,dr)$ is nowhere zero. Then the charged mass function $\varpi$ is
constant, say $m$. Around each point there are local
coordinates $(t,r)$ on the quotient in which
$$g=-f(r)\,dt^2+f(r)^{-1}\,dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad f(r)=1-\frac{2m}{r}+\frac{q_e^2+q_m^2}{r^2}-\frac{\Lambda r^2}{3},$$
and
$$\mathcal F=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dt\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$
For smooth vector fields $Y,V$ on an open set $O\subseteq\mathcal M$, define
their Lie bracket on $\varphi\in C^\infty(O)$ by
$[Y,V](\varphi):=Y(V(\varphi))-V(Y(\varphi))$. For a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ on $\mathcal M$ and smooth vector field $Y$,
define its Lie derivative by
$$(\mathcal L_Yh)(V,W):=Y(h(V,W))-h([Y,V],W)-h(V,[Y,W]),$$
for smooth vector fields $V,W$ on a common open set. A vector field is
**Killing** for $h$ when
$\mathcal L_Yh=0$. The quotient coordinate field $\partial_t$
has the product lift $K_{(y,p)}=(\partial_t|_y,0)$ to $\mathcal M$; this
lift is Killing for the full warped metric $g$ and has squared norm $-f$.
Where $f>0$, $K$ is timelike and is future- or past-directed according to the
given time orientation; where $f<0$, $K$ is spacelike and no future/past
designation is asserted. For $\Lambda=0$ this is the dyonic
Reissner–Nordström local form in the stated source convention.
Constant-radius and null-gradient patches, points with $f=0$, global
extensions, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, and black-hole uniqueness are
outside the claim.

items.statement:
Every exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–$\Lambda$ datum is locally expressible
in the charged Reissner–Nordström–(A)dS form with its areal radius $r$ as a
coordinate, without any restriction on $dr$.
